subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-level `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` core config surface now, and should it remain default-only or follow the newer per-agent bootstrap profile pattern too?
rationale: The code is bounded and proven, but choosing the public config shape affects prompt context, hook-loaded files, session behavior, and compatibility expectations in a way automation should not decide.

options.title: Sponsor the tier contract with docs
options.body: Proceed with this PR shape after maintainer review, requiring public docs, refreshed CI, and explicit acceptance of minimal/standard/full plus hook-extra semantics.

options.title: Fold into per-agent bootstrap profiles
options.body: Pause or replace this branch with a design that extends the current per-agent bootstrap override pattern instead of adding a default-only tier knob.

options.title: Decline the new knob
options.body: Close the PR and keep users on existing `contextInjection`, bootstrap budget, lightweight context, and per-agent override controls until a broader selector is designed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the tier contract with docs
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR shape after maintainer review, requiring public docs, refreshed CI, and explicit acceptance of minimal/standard/full plus hook-extra semantics.
